In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sinapic acid-based sunscreen molecules display an ultrafast photoprotection pathway, which is based on a primary relaxation mechanism, that involves the photoisomerization of the trans ground-state to the cis isomer.

the primary relaxation mechanism displayed in the sinapic acid derivative molecules investigated here can be described as a multi-step process involving internal conversion and photoisomerization of the initially photo-excited trans-1(1) ππ* state, leading to the formation of the trans ground-state isomers or cis photoisomers.
sinapoyl esters are not only capable of protecting the plant from UV light but can also protect the plant from visible light, which may be a new and unexpected property of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the primary relaxation mechanism of sinapoyl derivatives involves a trans-cis isomerization process that is ultrafast in the sub-picosecond time scale, and that the cis isomer may be formed as a stable species.
sinapic acid, sinapoyl glucose, sinapoylglycine and sinapoyl glutamate are all able to act as effective sunscreens in natural plants, as they all exhibit ultrafast photoprotection.
sinapic acid and its esters are capable of photoprotection in a wide range of solvents.

the photostability of these molecules may not be solely attributed to the absence of a 1(ππ*) absorption band in the visible region of the spectrum.
